analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: Desk (Privorotsky) says markets rebounded from a hard end to last week: KOSPI +2%, Tokyo Electron +5% after a beat and guidance for 87% operating profit growth, oil -3% on open diplomatic channels, Kioxia -15% again. The open debate is deteriorating AI economics versus forced liquidation of crowded positions.

The desk sees the market de-grossing AI longs. The GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate fell -2.17%, the worst weekly drawdown since Dec '23. Fundamental L/S nets recovered only to the seventh percentile, mostly through index short covering. Single stocks were net sold for a 7th straight week and Macro Products were net bought for a 2nd straight week (PB data).
Sentiment is reset: AAII Bull-Bear is negative again and CNN fear/greed is in the 20s. The desk says the market is less crowded this week than the week before.

Hyperscaler cloud growth: Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%. Negative FCF, equity raises and rising leverage raise return-on-capital questions. Intel fell -29% on Friday, which Privorotsky reads as consumer PC, margin and manufacturing weakness rather than AI demand. Amazon closed 1.4% lower after being down 7% pre-market.

Privorotsky says the AI debate is circular: one camp says power and data centers cannot support 2027 spending, the other says compute will be overproduced and hurt rental economics. Demand is strong but the return on the next trillion dollars of investment is less certain.
US midterms are tomorrow. The desk notes that equities have historically been positive after midterms because uncertainty is removed, and that much of the worry is already in positioning.
Oil/Iran: diplomacy through Qatar continues with no agreement. It is unclear whether the diplomatic window survives the elections. Privorotsky has no strong conviction.

Treasury QRA on Wednesday may be underappreciated. Smaller long-end auctions, more buybacks or a shift to bills would give duration relief and could help duration and growth equities. Unchanged issuance might disappoint on the margin. Long-end cuts were not explicitly raised in the dealer questionnaire.

BoE Thursday: a 25bp hike to 4% is almost fully priced. The desk thinks the three to four further hikes priced over the next year look aggressive given weakening growth, and leans toward the market overpricing the full tightening cycle. Energy inflation is the risk.

Week ahead: ISM manufacturing and Apple tonight, AMD tomorrow (critical after Intel), Arista for AI networking, and NFP Friday with consensus around +65k, unemployment 4.2% and wages +0.3%. Privorotsky expects a painful year-end rally that is under-owned, poorly participated in and hard to chase, once events clear.

Pasquariello: S&P fell 57bps last week but the momentum basket GSPRHIMO had monthly returns of -30.19% (July), -13.67% (Aug), +26.96% (Sep), -18.60% (Oct) against S&P -0.13%, +2.62%, -0.45%, -0.93%. The index masks large single stock, sector and thematic moves.
Pasquariello's view: the primary bull trend is intact, but with less upside power, and sub-surface volatility is here to stay. He is not making big bets right now.

Pasquariello: Q3 tech earnings will be remembered as a disappointment even though hyperscaler capex intentions are not slowing. S&P earnings growth appears to have peaked and the pace of upgrades to forward estimates has slowed.

Pasquariello sees the technicals favoring bulls over the next two months: sentiment is downbeat, seasonality turns from the worst stretch of the year to the best, and the market has cleared a large amount of length. Bears could note the same was said in late 2018.

Pasquariello: oil has built risk premium into the midterms (COZ6 on its dead highs) while European equities rose again and SMI hit record highs. He agrees with raising commodity allocations, with BCOM +28% YTD, and notes GS made tactical and structural bull cases. The 4th largest company in the index had its worst day ever.

Coppersmith: the GS Risk Appetite Indicator had its largest drop since November 2021 but is not at levels that have marked contrarian buying opportunities. After the 11 largest RAI declines since 2005, S&P outcomes ranged from -17% to +7% over 1 month and -32% to +18% over 6 months.

Hedge fund performance in October: Fundamental L/S -3.5%, systematic L/S -3.6% including -2.5% last week. Gross exposure is 314% (97th percentile over 5 years) and net is in the 10th percentile over 1 year. Fundamental L/S beta-adjusted net hit a 1-year low, so high leverage remains a source of volatility.
Institutions remain short VIX futures but have covered aggressively in the last couple of weeks, nearly matching Q1.

Earnings are not the problem: with 60% of the S&P reported, EPS growth is tracking +33% y/y and 70% of stocks have risen since earnings season began. The reaction in the largest, best-owned names, especially hyperscalers, has been weak.

AI financing: hyperscaler capex is expected at $1.2tn in 2027, aggregate FCF turned negative in Q3 and upward earnings revisions are moderating. GS Research says the funding gap may be smaller than feared: Oracle plans ~$220bn of AI spending and expects to raise $20bn through 2030, and GS Credit estimates the bond market could absorb ~$500bn more hyperscaler debt. Microsoft's AI development platform is growing +300% y/y.

The Fed was a sideshow, with Warsh striking a measured tone and GIR still expecting a hike in December. AI-related equity volatility has overtaken energy as a key driver of bond yields. Investors are underweight Treasuries, so yields have room to fall if risk-off continues.

Midterms: Democrats are above 90% to take the House. GIR sees limited immediate market effects. Divided government makes major policy change unlikely, with higher tariffs (~2pts on the effective rate) and the Dec 11 funding deadline as the bigger risks. GS thinks fears of a data center regulatory crackdown are overdone.

Garrett: SPX 12-month implied correlation is around 20%, one of the lowest levels in history, so 2027 is priced as one of the most dispersive years. SPX rose ~150bps and NDX ~300bps Mon-Wed, then NDX fell 140bps Thursday and 350bps Friday.

Garrett's contra-indicators: macro equity vol is starting to show nervousness, net exposure is rising through short covering, downside volatility now exceeds upside volatility in large caps, and SPX forward P/E is ~19x, the lowest of 2026 even with SPX +10.7% YTD.
Factor extremes (10-year percentiles): dividend yield factor in the 90th, valuation factor 80th, momentum 30th and growth 40th, so safe is expensive and growth and momentum are cheap.

Prime brokerage: hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in four weeks, largely macro short covering. TMT was the most bought sector on the week but is heavily sold month to date, while Mag7 length remains near YTD highs. The desk regressed PB net levels against SPX drawdowns and finds the current level has been associated with >20% drawdowns.

Cash desk sold a net $4.2bn of tech delta on Friday, with a nearly $10bn peak-to-trough skew in the week. CTAs: SPX closed 35 handles above the medium-term threshold and NDX closed below both thresholds, and the desk expects red across systematics on Monday.

Derivatives: gamma has not repriced like vol and skew, 0DTE straddles stayed steady, and Wednesday's SPX straddle covering AAPL earnings and the midterms costs 30bps less than Friday's single-session move (150bps implied vs -180bps realized). Friday's US option volume was close to 100 million contracts, the fourth highest session on record.
Year-end straddles through 42 remaining sessions: SPX +/-5.1%, NDX +/-7.8%, RTY +/-6.3%. Large cap vol exceeds small cap vol.
Baskets: the desk has pair trades for health insurance affordability, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending and corporate tax beneficiaries around the midterms.

AMD reports tomorrow and is called critical after Intel's warning.
Apple reports tonight. The desk calls it a relatively defensive tech name and watches iPhone demand and early Duo orders.
Arista is a useful read on AI networking this week.
Kioxia fell another 15%, showing the rebound is not indiscriminate. No US listing is given.
